channel.title: Tyler's Treks
channel.description: Exploring every California national park in 2026, camping out of a truck.

item.title: December 11, 2025 — White Cross World War I Memorial, Nipton, California
item.description: The first night in the camper shell! I drove up to Nipton, CA and camped out right next to [White Cross World War I Memorial](https://maps.app.goo.gl/q6prwbHUXk6rEk8L7). The spot was perfect for my first time, plenty of free camping spots and some great trails nearby.

item.title: December 13, 2025 — Hole-in-the-Wall Campground, Essex, California
item.description: Second outing was definitely lazier in the setup. After getting cleaned out by Vegas, I drove up to Essex, CA and camped out near [Hole in the Wall Campground](https://maps.app.goo.gl/atCuCDzLRG7YN7HE8). By the time I got there, I was cooked so I just laid in my sleeping bag and used my sweatshirts as a pillow.

item.title: January 1, 2026 — Pinnacle Road, Trona, California
item.description: Happy New Year! Drove out 3 hours around sunset to Trona Pinnacles. I should have left a wee bit earlier as it was tough to navigate in the dark. I stopped about 5 miles short on a random dirt road off of Pinnacle Road. My truck felt the effect of the rain on the dirt roads these past couple weeks.

item.title: January 2, 2026 — Trona and Ridgecrest, California
item.description: Oh boy. Buckle up for this one. Woke up at 6 am because I was worrying about the mud pit I had driven through the night before. I wanted to just get through it as early as possible in case anything went wrong. And in fact, everything went wrong. I tried to be sneaky and cut around the water that I barely made it through the night before and ended up getting stuck in a mud pit. I did everything you aren't supposed to do when you're in mud. I floored it in drive, floored it in reverse, turned my tires every which way. After I had dug myself deeper in the mud pit, I found some wood left by others who had also gotten stuck but were able to get out. I tried shimmying those under my tires and giving it another go. Did it work? Absolutely not.

item.title: January 3, 2026 — Death Valley National Park, California
item.description: Today was the big hiking day. First hike of the day was [Mosaic Canyon](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/california/mosaic-canyon-trail). Very beautiful, like being on the moon with the black gravel. Second hike was [Golden Canyon](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/california/golden-canyon-trail-and-badlands-loop-to-zabriskie-point). This one was the bee's knees. Rock slabs were incredible. The last hike of the day was the [Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/california/mesquite-flat-sand-dunes-trail) right before sunset.

item.title: January 4, 2026 — Badwater Road, Death Valley National Park, California
item.description: Wrapped up the trip with a drive down Badwater Road to see [Badwater Basin](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/california/badwater-basin-salt-flats-trail), Lake Manly, and [Artist's Palette](https://www.alltrails.com/explore/poi/us/california/death-valley/artists-palette).

item.title: May 8, 2026 — Black Rock Canyon Campground, Joshua Tree National Park, California
item.description: The second NP I hit this year was Joshua Tree. I went into the park immediately and did the Hidden Valley loop. A nice time scrambling around on some of the rock formations. Made camp at Black Rock Campground, located about 35 mins from the park entrance. My friends joined me on this trip which most definitely added to the fun. It's a lot easier to play monopoly deal and a lot less sad drinking a beer when I'm not out there all alone. The campsite was great, places to fill water, nice views of the rolling hills, even a snake found its way to our site!

item.title: May 9, 2026 — Hidden Valley Trail, Joshua Tree National Park, California
item.description: The next day we went into the park and did the Chasm of Doom trail near Hidden Valley trailhead. To say I had a tough time finding the entrance was an understatement — I led us into multiple crevices that just dead ended. But luckily some hikers who were also looking for some doom decided to take the lead after watching us walk in circles for 30 minutes. The hike was epic, more climbing and scrambling than an actual hike. Joshua Tree has definitely been my favorite so far. The scrambling out there is unbelievable, it's truly an adult playground.

item.title: May 17, 2026 — Sulfur Works & Mill Creek Resort, Lassen Volcanic National Park, California
item.description: Drove up to Lassen to begin the big trip! This trip I was going to hit the 2 most northern parks from me, Redwoods and Lassen Volcanic. Once I got there, I went into the park and checked out Sulfur Works. It didn't do much for me, a bit smelly for my liking. The surrounding area was beautiful though. Unfortunately the main highway through the park was closed to cars which made exploring the greater part a bit more manual than I had expected. On the way up I acquired a tent from REI for my camper — no more tarp for this guy!

item.title: May 18, 2026 — Mill Creek Falls Trail & Highway 89, Lassen Volcanic, California
item.description: I began the day with the most mediocre dehydrated meal I think I've ever had. With a stomach full of the best coffee ever and whatever crime you would call wet milk granola soup, I was bound towards Mill Creek Falls. With it being so early in the season, there was nobody on the trail and the deer were taking full advantage. I've never seen so many in my life. Knowing that the main highway to get around was closed to cars, I rented a bike and rode Highway 89 about 5 miles up. Being the only one on the highway and getting to see the views was pretty surreal.

item.title: May 19, 2026 — Mill Creek Trail, Stout Grove & Grove of Titans — Jedediah Smith Redwoods, California
item.description: Driving from Lassen took about 6 hours — I took the way through Oregon just to say I went to Oregon. I got there earlier than my campsite reservation so I headed over to Stout Grove. Grove of Titans was gorgeous, giant redwoods. I took Mill Creek Trail from Grove of Titans back to Stout Grove. This route was one I would definitely take again — you see all the mega trees and then it opens up to a really nice creek where you can swim and hang. The photos don't really capture the sheer size, it's something everyone should see at some point.

item.title: May 20, 2026 — James Irvine Trail, Fern Canyon & Simpson-Reed Trail — Prairie Creek Redwoods, California
item.description: Big day. Made oatmeal and coffee in the morning and drove down the 101. The NP ranger gave me a lot of great recommendations so I tried doing as many as possible. The James Irvine to Fern Canyon to Clintonia to Miner's Ridge hike was a beast — not hard but long for sure. You start off walking through beautiful behemoths of redwoods and then it spits you out into a little creek canyon. I think Jurassic Park was filmed there so just imagine velociraptors hiding in the trees. I was on the trail by 7 on a Wednesday so it was near empty, which made it feel even more surreal.

item.title: May 21, 2026 — Ten Taypo–Hope Creek Loop & Avenue of Giants, Humboldt Redwoods, California
item.description: I began my departure from Redwoods by taking the scenic route. On my way down, I stopped by for one more hike at Ten Taypo–Hope Creek Loop off of Newton Scenic Parkway. Easy hike, nobody around, really beautiful and a nice sendoff to wrap up this adventure. I made one final stop in Prairie Creek Redwoods to check out the Big Tree. I confirmed that the Big Tree is in fact Big. From there I headed down the 101 and took State Route 254 to check out the Avenue of Giants. And with that wrapped up the week long adventure. 4 parks down, 5 more to go!
